title: Catching Up: A Conversation About Life, Work and Progress

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Kamila! I haven't seen you for ages. How's everything?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Good — busy. I've been working on my thesis since September. It's been taking over my life.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Language and identity in Kazakhstani higher education. I've interviewed twelve students so far.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: That sounds fascinating. Have you found anything surprising?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Yes — I've discovered that students switch languages mid-sentence much more than I expected. I've been analysing the patterns.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: I've noticed that myself. I've been doing it since I started at WKU.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Exactly. And I've found that the patterns aren't random — they depend on the topic and the relationship between speakers.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Have you written anything yet? Or is it all still in the analysis phase?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I've written the introduction and the methodology. But I've been struggling with the findings chapter — it keeps growing.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: How many words have you written overall?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: About 8,000. But I've rewritten about 3,000 of those. And I've been reading so much that my desk is buried in papers.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: You've made good progress though. How long have you been working on it?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Six months. It feels like six years.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: What about you — how has your year been?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Good question. I've been learning a lot. And I've finally started to enjoy the process — which I haven't always done.
